title: What is five quarters times three halves?
description: The video multiplies five quarters by three halves with a unit square as the whole, taking one quarter of three halves first and then five of those. Keeko then raises a hand with the doubt that the tops and the bottoms can be added.
teaching_notes: One idea: one quarter of three halves is three eighths, and five of those make fifteen eighths. Watch for students who add the tops and add the bottoms, which gives an answer smaller than three halves.

source: Multiply 5/4 × 3/2, using a unit square as the whole.
video_script.why: The child has found a fraction of a fraction in a unit square and now takes a fraction larger than one whole of a fraction larger than one whole.
video_script.substitution: One quarter of three halves is three eighths, and five of those make fifteen eighths.
video_script.anchor: Multiply five quarters by three halves, using a unit square as the whole
video_script.wrong_move: adds the tops, five and three, and the bottoms, four and two, and gets eight sixths, which is smaller than three halves
video_script.payoff_line: Five quarters times three halves is fifteen eighths, which is one and seven eighths

final_answer.spoken: fifteen eighths, which is one and seven eighths

video_script.fraction_reading: five quarters, three halves, one quarter, three eighths, fifteen eighths, one and seven eighths, eight sixths
maths_rules: 3/2 = one whole square and half of a second square
1/4 of 3/2: the whole is cut into 2 rows and 4 columns, 2 × 4 = 8 equal parts, with 3 shaded, so 3/8
the slip: 8/6 is less than 3/2, though 5/4 is more than 1 and the product must be more than 3/2
video_script.design: One idea: take one quarter of three halves, then five of those. The unit square with the three halves shaded is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is eight sixths.
Keeko added the tops, five and three, and added the bottoms, four and two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But five quarters is more than one whole.
The answer must be more than three halves, and eight sixths is less.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Take one quarter of three halves first, and then take five of those parts.
